passages.title: 33번 지문
passages.text: Some people argue that there is a single, logically consistent concept known as reading that can be neatly set apart from everything else people do with books. Is reading really that simple? The most productive way to think about reading is as a collection of activities in which many other opinions interact owing to family resemblances, as Ludwig Wittgenstein used the phrase, without having in common a single defining trait. Consequently, efforts to distinguish reading from nonreading are destined to fail because there is no agreement on what qualifies as reading in the first place. The more one tries to figure out where the border lies between reading and not-reading, the more edge cases will be found to stretch the term's flexible boundaries. Thus, it is worth attempting to collect together these exceptional forms of reading into a single forum, one highlighting the challenges faced by anyone wishing to establish the boundaries where reading begins and ends. The attempt moves toward an understanding of reading as a spectrum that is expansive enough to accommodate the distinct reading activities.

questions.context:

(A) Consequently, efforts to distinguish reading from nonreading are destined to fail because there is no agreement on what qualifies as reading in the first place. The more one tries to figure out where the border lies between reading and not-reading, the more edge cases will be found to stretch the term's flexible boundaries.

(B) Is reading really that simple? The most productive way to think about reading is as a loosely related set of behaviors that belong together owing to family resemblances, as Ludwig Wittgenstein used the phrase, without having in common a single defining trait.

(C) Thus, it is worth attempting to collect together these exceptional forms of reading into a single forum, one highlighting the challenges faced by anyone wishing to establish the boundaries where reading begins and ends. questions.explanation:
②
[해설]
주어진 글은 '읽기'는 깔끔하게 분리될 수 있는 유일하고 논리적으로 일관성 있는 개념이라고 주장하는 사람들에게 글쓴이가 (B) '읽기가 그렇게 단순한 게 맞는지' 의문점을 제기하며, 읽기를 이해하기 위해서는 서로 유사한 행동들이 모여 있는 연결된 행동의 묶음으로 바라봐야 한다고 하고 있다. 그래서 (A) 결국(Consequently) 읽기와 읽기가 아닌 것을 구분하려는 노력은 결국 실패할 수밖에 없다고 주장한다. 그러면서 '읽기와 읽기가 아닌 것 사이의 경계를 알 수 없는 특이 사례들'에 대한 이야기를 하고 있다. (C) 그러므로(Thus) 뒤에 나오는 '이러한 예외적인 읽기의 형태들'은 앞의 문장에서 설명한 '읽기와 읽기가 아닌 것 사이의 경계를 알 수 없는 특이 사례들'을 가리키고 있고, '읽기'에 대한 포괄적인 이해를 돕고, 다양한 형태의 읽기를 이해할 수 있게 한다는 내용으로 이어진다.

questions.text: Some people argue that there is a single, logically consistent concept known as reading that can be neatly set apart from everything else people do with books. Is reading really that ⓐ (s-) {{simple}}? The most productive way to think about reading is as a loosely related set of behaviors that belong together owing to family resemblances, as Ludwig Wittgenstein used the phrase, without having in common a single defining trait. Consequently, efforts to distinguish reading from nonreading are destined to ⓑ (f-) {{fail}} because there is no agreement on what ⓒ (q-) {{qualifies}} as reading in the first place. The more one tries to figure out where the border lies between reading and not-reading, the more edge cases will be found to stretch the term's ⓓ (f-) {{flexible}} boundaries. Thus, it is worth attempting to collect together these exceptional forms of reading into a single forum, one highlighting the challenges faced by anyone wishing to establish the boundaries where reading begins and ends. The attempt moves toward an understanding of reading as a spectrum that is ⓔ (e-) {{expansive}} enough to accommodate the distinct reading activities.
